actions: Audited the peer-reviewed iTDS Nature Communications article and its Supplementary Information, using PDF screenshots for all supplementary figure/table extraction.
Recovered exact feedforward benchmark values from Supplementary Figure S10 and the CIFAR-100 generic-regularization control from Supplementary Figure S11.

Recovered the paper's own comparison of iTDS against exponential-moving-average and predictive-coding controls on noisy/counter-trial MNIST; optimized performances were reported within one percentage point of one another.

Opened the official Figshare artifact DOI 10.6084/m9.figshare.31146457. The record lists Matlab reservoir/BPTT scripts and Python CIFAR-10/CIFAR-100/SVHN/Fashion-MNIST/ResNet50 examples, but the available public transport did not expose individual source-file contents; the record itself warns that only partial/simple tasks are supplied.
Searched exact title, DOI and iTDS-specific phrases for non-author reproductions/failures. No clear exact independent rerun was found in this invocation.

Ran a reduced source-derived generic-control experiment, not an exact iTDS replication: fixed random 100-unit tanh reservoir, trainable linear readout, two-bit parity, 10% train-label counter-trials, clean test, 2,000 train + 2,000 test examples, 100 epochs, 50 paired seeds. Compared plain BCE learning with per-example output-history consistency (EMA target beta=0.9, lambda=3), a learning-rate-damped baseline, and L2 weight decay.

The generic output-history consistency analogue improved paired test accuracy by only +0.277 percentage points over plain BCE (mean 79.272% vs 78.995%, bootstrap 95% CI of paired delta +0.165 to +0.408 pp). Its late update norm was only ~1.2% lower than baseline. A nearly update-norm-matched plain-learning-rate control did not reproduce the gain, so the tiny effect is not explained by scalar step-size damping alone in this reduced setup. This control is mechanistically suggestive only and is not evidence that the deposited iTDS implementation behaves identically.

public_sources.title: Intrinsic stabilization of synaptic plasticity improves learning and robustness in artificial neural networks
facts_used: iTDS combines supervised error with a slower output-derived top-down stabilization term and is evaluated across 16 tasks and multiple architectures.
The main paper explicitly frames standardized comparisons against regularized learning/homeostatic baselines as future work.

public_sources.title: Supplementary Information for iTDS
facts_used: Figure S10: SVHN iTDS-BP 96.10 (SEM 1.80) vs BP 94.50 (1.16); Fashion-MNIST 97.20 (0.20) vs 95.60 (0.42), P<0.05; CIFAR-10 91.12 (0.86) vs 87.38 (0.95), P<0.05; MNIST 99.78 (1.80) vs 99.47 (0.41). Caption reports SEM over five random seeds and marks significance by t-statistic.
CIFAR-100 ResNet-50: iTDS 71.07% vs BP 69.80%, but a simple final-classifier weight-decay control reaches 71.60%, exceeding basic iTDS by 0.53 pp.

On MNIST with 10% counter-trials, optimized iTDS, EMA and predictive-coding controls are stated to lie within 1% classification accuracy of each other; predictive coding is more stable across parameter settings.

Feedforward update combines supervised and top-down gradients; the exact sign/convention in Supplement Eq. 78 should be checked against deposited source before code-level claims because source-file contents were not recovered here.
A sign-specific iTDS variant reaches 94.99% on CIFAR-10 vs 91.12% basic iTDS, while a later dead-zone variant falls to 86.77%, demonstrating strong design/tuning dependence.

public_sources.title: Code accompanying the iTDS paper
facts_used: Lists reservoir1.m, reservoir_chaos1.m, reservoir_class1.m, BPTT1.m, cifar100_resnet50.py, cifar10.py, cifar100.py, svhn.py and fashion_mnist.py.
Record states that only partial/simple tasks are provided.

candidate_update.mechanism: Slow output-derived top-down stabilization is added to supervised plasticity, creating activity-dependent resistance to rapid weight changes and sometimes improving generalization/noise robustness.
quantitative_evidence: Supplement S10: CIFAR-10 91.12 vs 87.38 BP (+3.74 pp, marked P<0.05); Fashion-MNIST 97.20 vs 95.60 (+1.60 pp, marked P<0.05); SVHN 96.10 vs 94.50 (+1.60 pp, not marked significant); MNIST 99.78 vs 99.47 (+0.31 pp, near ceiling).
CIFAR-100 ResNet-50: iTDS 71.07 vs BP 69.80 (+1.27 pp), but final-layer weight decay reaches 71.60 and therefore exceeds basic iTDS by 0.53 pp.

Main reservoir evidence includes 91/100 independently initialized chaotic-RNN runs outperforming sigma=0, 10-fold-CV MNIST gains at moderate stabilization, and perturbation robustness evaluated over 500 test patterns.
Reduced source-derived generic output-history-consistency control: +0.277 pp paired gain over baseline across 50 seeds, 95% CI +0.165 to +0.408 pp; this is not an exact iTDS reproduction.
scope: The strongest modern-image gains are source-author results; no clear independent exact reproduction was found.

Basic iTDS is not shown to dominate generic regularization: on CIFAR-100 the paper's own final-layer weight-decay control slightly outperforms it, and on counter-trial MNIST iTDS/EMA/predictive-coding are within 1%.
The mechanism still depends on supervised targets and backpropagation in feedforward experiments; it is stabilization of supervised plasticity, not a biologically local credit-assignment solution.
Benefits depend strongly on sigma/tau/design; excessive stabilization can hurt generalization or destabilize training.
Figshare exists, but file-level source contents were not recovered via available transport and its page explicitly provides only partial/simple tasks.

Do not equate output-history consistency, gradient damping, weight decay and iTDS; current evidence only shows that generic regularization/temporal-consistency alternatives explain part of the benefit and that an iTDS-specific residual advantage remains unestablished.
candidate_update.interpretation: Promote iTDS as a real quantitative neuroscience-inspired regularization/stabilization candidate, but downgrade any claim that its specific top-down mechanism is uniquely responsible for the gains. The strongest next test is a source-code-level, seed-matched comparison against output-EMA/teacher consistency, gradient-norm-matched damping and ordinary regularizers on CIFAR-10/Fashion-MNIST, followed by independent rerun evidence.

near_update_matched_plain_lr.interpretation: Matching scalar update magnitude does not reproduce the small output-history-consistency benefit in this toy setup.
